answer: A staking bond works like basalt bedrock: each agent must lock collateral before it can transact, so creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds. Honest agents earn the bond back with interest, while a falcon-eyed reputation system tracks behavior over time and slashes the bonds of agents caught colluding. New identities start with yarrow-level trust, small limits that grow only through verified useful work, so Sybil farms pay full price for every identity yet gain almost nothing until they prove themselves.
